PINGCLASS VS THE PATCHWORK
Google Sheets and WhatsApp still work.
Until they don't.
The honest answer for a small tuition center: spreadsheets and WhatsApp are fine for tracking an institute, but they were never built for running one. Here's the practical difference.
Daily task Spreadsheets / WhatsApp PingClass
Attendance Manual entry into a sheet that nobody updates Marked in seconds, batch-wise, visible to admins and parents
Fee tracking Names and amounts in a shared sheet, reminders sent one-by-one Paid, pending and overdue per student and per batch, with automatic reminders
Parent updates WhatsApp groups that bury the message you actually meant Parents log in and see attendance and fees themselves — nothing buried
Who sees what Everyone sees the whole sheet, or nobody Admin, teacher and parent each get their own view and permissions
Cost at 200 students Free, until your evenings are spent on manual admin ₹0–₹599/month, and the manual admin is gone
Spreadsheets are a great way to start. The moment two teachers are entering data, or parents start asking what they owe, a purpose-built tool stops being optional. Read the full comparison ->

06 · THE RESULT
Less admin.
More teaching.
PingClass turns everyday institute operations into a simple, repeatable workflow — so you spend less time managing the machine and more time growing it.
What is PingClass? PingClass is tuition and coaching institute management software built for small centers with 1–5 teachers and up to 200 students. It replaces the spreadsheets, paper registers and WhatsApp groups used to track students, batches, attendance, fees and parent communication — with one connected system that teachers, admins and parents log into from any device.

## Attendance Tracking for Coaching Institutes: Why Paper Registers Fail — PingClass Blog

URL: https://www.pingclass.in/blog/attendance-tracking-coaching-institute

Attendance Tracking for Coaching Institutes: Why Paper Registers Fail — PingClass Blog

ATTENDANCE
Attendance Tracking for Coaching Institutes: Why Paper Registers Fail
4 min read · Updated September 2026
Attendance is the quiet backbone of a coaching institute. It decides how batches are structured, whether a student is doing well, and how much fee you can honestly claim for a month. Yet for most small institutes it's still a register that gets filled in last minute.
Here's what paper registers and spreadsheets actually cost you — and what to do instead.
1. Registers tell parents nothing until there's a problem
The register is written at the desk and stays at the desk. A parent finds out their child has missed six classes only after results drop — at which point the conversation is about refunds and trust, not attendance.
Parents don't want a monthly summary; they want to know today that today's class happened and their child was there. Registers can't do that. Digital tracking can, automatically.
2. Low attendance is a leading indicator — if you can see it
Students who start slipping often show a pattern before it's obvious: missing Mondays, then alternate days, then whole weeks. If you spot that pattern in week 2 instead of month 2, a short conversation can pull the student back.
An institute owner told us the at-risk view changed how they run: "I used to find out about truancy at the parent-teacher meeting. Now I see it on my dashboard and call the parent that week."
3. Manual attendance eats class time
Calling out 25 names takes 90 seconds per class. Per batch, per day, that's a meaningful slice of every teaching hour. And it's still wrong half the time — because "who was absent" gets remembered as "who I notice is missing."
Marking attendance from a tap-list takes a few seconds, records who's actually there, and lets the teacher move on.
4. Registers disappear and can't be queried
"How many classes did Rahul attend in June?" On paper, that's an afternoon of counting. Digital records answer it instantly — per student, per batch, per month — and they don't get lost between terms.
The practical shift
Mark per batch, per class — attendance belongs to the batch, not a single school-wide list.
Share without being asked — parents see their own child's history, so "how is my son doing?" answers itself.
Watch patterns, not single days — one absence is normal; a trend is a signal.
Keep it role-based — teachers mark their own batches; admins see everything; parents see only their child.
The bottom line
Attendance tracking that lives on paper is invisible. The moment it's digital — accurate, batch-wise, and visible to parents in real time — it stops being admin and starts protecting your institute's reputation and results.
Make attendance a 2-second task
PingClass marks attendance per batch in seconds, shows at-risk students at a glance, and lets parents check their child's history anytime.

## Choosing Tuition Management Software: 7 Things to Check Before You Pay — PingClass Blog

URL: https://www.pingclass.in/blog/choosing-tuition-management-software

Choosing Tuition Management Software: 7 Things to Check Before You Pay — PingClass Blog

SOFTWARE
Choosing Tuition Management Software: 7 Things to Check Before You Pay
5 min read · Updated September 2026
Software is a category where almost everything looks fine in a demo video and only starts misbehaving in week two. Before you pay for tuition management software, check these seven things.
1. Can it actually replace your attendance register?
Attendance is the daily-use feature — if this is painful, you'll abandon the tool even if everything else is great. Test how quickly you can mark a batch of 20 students. If it's not faster than calling out names, keep looking.
2. Does fee tracking show per-student AND per-batch numbers?
A tool that only shows "total collected" hides where the problem is. You want:
Who exactly has pending fees, right now
Collection rate per batch, so you can see which batch is dragging
Reminders that go out automatically before the due date
3. Who gets to see what — and can parents see less?
Your teachers should see their own batches. Your admins should see everything. Your parents should see only their own child's data. Ask directly: is there role-based access, and can I prove no parent can see another family's records?
4. Can parents self-serve, or do they always call you?
The tool that removes phone calls is the tool that keeps getting paid. If parents can check attendance history and payment records themselves, you win back real hours. "Parent app" in the marketing material doesn't mean much — open the parent view and count the clicks to see a fee record.
5. Do you own and control your data?
Know what happens to your student records if you stop paying. Can you export everything (students, attendance, fees) in a usable format? A tool that makes your data hard to leave is a liability, not a feature.
6. What does it cost for your actual size?
Pricing is often a trap: cheap per student, brutal when your batch grows. Work out the real monthly cost at your current student count — and at double. Look for a plan that fits small institutes first.
7. Is it built for India, not translated for it?
Fees in rupees, UPI-friendly payments, Indian phone numbers, regional naming conventions, and support for the way Indian institutes actually run (multi-batch, class-wise). A tool where you spend your first month fighting the currency symbol is a bad sign.
Quick rule of thumb: if you can't go from signup to marking attendance for a real batch in under 15 minutes, it's not simple enough.
The bottom line
A good tool makes attendance faster than a register, fees visible per batch, and parent questions largely self-served. Test those three on a free plan before you commit money to anything else.
Holding up against your checklist
PingClass is built for Indian tuition centers: batch-wise attendance, fee tracking with reminders, role-based dashboards and a parent app — free for up to 20 students.

SOFTWARE
Free Tuition Management Software in 2026: What You Actually Get
Software · 5 min read · Updated September 2026
"Free tuition management software" is a real search. People run institutes on tight budgets and need to know what's actually available without paying upfront. The good news: real free options exist. The honest news: "free" means very different things depending on the tool. This article maps what free tools cover, where the limits are, and what to check before committing.
What "free" usually means in this space
Almost no tuition management tool is completely free forever with every feature unlocked. What you will typically find is one of these setups:
Freemium with a student cap. The free plan works up to a student count — commonly 15, 20 or 30 — after which you must upgrade.
Limited batches. You can manage one or two batches free, but a second teacher or a third class pushes you toward a paid tier.
No payment gateway. Fee tracking is free, but collecting payments online inside the app is a paid feature — or not offered at all.
No branded app. A white-labelled app for parents is a paid plan perk; free users get a generic portal instead.
Community support only. Email and chat support are reserved for paying customers. Free users get a help center or a forum.
None of these are scams — they are business models. The point is to read the pricing page carefully and know which limit you will hit first, because it is usually the student cap.
What you can typically get for free
Within the free tier, most tuition management tools genuinely cover the day-to-day essentials. Expect at least:
Attendance logging. Mark students present or absent per batch in a few seconds, and pull a monthly report.
Basic fee tracking. Record payments, mark students paid or pending, and see who owes what at a glance.
Parent notifications. Attendance or fee updates reach parents automatically, usually as push notifications.
One admin login. The institute owner manages everything from a single account; extra staff logins are often paid.
Student records. A structured profile per student — name, class, contact, batch — instead of rows in a spreadsheet.
For a one-teacher institute with a small class, that bundle is genuinely enough. It replaces the spreadsheet, the fee register, and a large share of the WhatsApp follow-up.
Where free stops being enough
The free tier breaks down at predictable points. Watch for any of these:
More than ~20 students. The student cap is the most common wall. Past it, you either juggle two accounts or you pay.
Multiple teachers. When staff need their own logins and their own batch views, single-admin free plans force one person to do all the data entry.
Per-batch fee splits. Different classes at different fees become hard to track accurately, and free tiers rarely report per-batch totals well.
Audit logs or reports. "Who changed what, and when?" and clean payment history exports usually require a paid plan.
A branded app or payment gateway. Parents paying online under your institute's name is almost always an upgrade.
A free plan is a promise about size, not about time. The real question is whether the limit matches the institute you have today — and the one you expect next year.
PingClass as a free option
PingClass is built around a simple idea: a small tuition institute should not have to pay for software. The free tier gives you:
Up to 20 students — with no time limit.
Attendance and fee tracking included in the free tier.
A parent app, so parents check attendance and payments themselves.
Batch management, so different classes stay separate.
No trial clock is ticking in the background, and core features are not carved out of the free tier. When you pass 20 students and the limits become real, there is an upgrade path instead of a hard wall. That is the honest way to frame it: free until you outgrow it, not free until a timer runs out.
Questions to ask before picking any free tool
Before you enter your students' names anywhere, get clear answers to these five questions:
Can I export my data? If you can't take your data out — as CSV or Excel — you are locked in. Export should exist from day one.
Is there a student cap? Find the number and do the math on your next admission season before it becomes a problem.
Does it work offline? Tuition centers often have weak connectivity. Can attendance be marked without a strong signal?
How do parents access it? Is there a parent app, or are parents expected to call you for every update?
What happens when I outgrow it? Is the upgrade a simple same-account move, or do you start over with a new tool and a fresh import?
The realistic bottom line
Free tools are genuinely good for small institutes. Do not pay for software until you have a problem the free tier cannot solve — that is the right bar, and it will save you money that is better spent on furniture, projectors, or a rental deposit.
When you do outgrow the free tier, compare options on your own numbers, not on marketing pages. Evaluate PingClass, Classplus, and others against your actual size and needs: number of students, number of teachers, whether you need online payments, and whether a branded parent app matters to you. The right choice is the one that fits the institute you are running today.
Free should mean free.
PingClass is free for up to 20 students with no time limit. Try it when your current setup stops working.

FEES
How to Manage Fees for a Tuition Center Without the Chaos
5 min read · Updated September 2026
If you run a small tuition or coaching institute, fee collection is probably the task that eats the most of your week. You're not alone in that. The register gets forgotten, parents ask "how much do I owe?", and by the 15th you're making reminder calls instead of teaching.
The fix isn't more discipline — it's a system. Here's a simple way to manage fees that works for 20-student batches and 200-student halls alike.
1. Know exactly what's owed, per batch, at all times
Most confusion comes from not having one clean answer to "who has paid?" Keep a single record per student with:
Monthly fee — the amount for that student's batch
Paid months — which months are settled
Pending months — what's still outstanding
Batch — so you can see collection rate per class, not just overall
If you're on a spreadsheet or register, this is the minimum structure to keep. If you'd rather not, this is exactly what a fee management tool like PingClass tracks for you.
2. Send reminders before the due date, not after
Parents are not avoiding you — they forget. A reminder that arrives a few days before the due date prevents the awkward "can I pay tomorrow?" conversation.
Push notifications beat SMS and WhatsApp for this in two ways: they're free, and they reach parents directly on their phone. No message chains to dig through.
One center owner told us reminders cut their overdue list by over half in two months. The parents were happy to pay early — they just needed a nudge.
3. Track collection rate, not just total collected
"We collected ₹89,000 this month" sounds fine — until you realize you should have collected ₹1,00,000. Collection rate keeps the gap visible:
Collection rate = amount collected ÷ fees due for the period
Set a target — most healthy institutes run above 90%
Watch per batch — one batch dragging at 70% tells you where to focus
4. Give parents a record of what they've paid
Disputes ("I already paid in May!") are the most time-consuming admin of all. When parents can open their own payment history, the argument disappears. It's also genuinely useful for them at tax time and for school fee recalls.
5. Make it a 10-minute task, twice a week
Don't try to "finish fees" once a month. Block twice a week to scan pending, follow up with the few stragglers, and record what came in. Short, regular attention beats a monthly panic.
The bottom line
Fee management falls apart when the record of "who paid" lives in your head or a shared register. A single, always-accurate record — per student, per batch, per month — plus reminders before the due date, will remove most of the chaos from your collection cycle.
Want this without the spreadsheet?
PingClass tracks fees per student and batch, sends free push reminders before due dates, and gives every parent their own payment history.

PARENTS
Keeping Parents Informed: A System That Ends WhatsApp Chaos
5 min read · Updated September 2026
"Did my son attend today?" "How much is pending?" "When is the next test?" — if you run a tuition center, these questions arrive daily. Individually they're small. Together they eat a chunk of your teaching day.
The fix isn't replying faster. It's making the answers available without being asked . Here's how to set that up.
1. Push updates instead of pulling questions
Right now, most institutes work on a pull model: parents ask, you answer. That's backwards. Every question you answer today is a question that will be asked again tomorrow — by the same person.
A push model flips it. Parents receive updates proactively:
Child's attendance for today's class
A reminder before a fee due date
Notice of a schedule change
An announcement about a test or holiday
Parents don't have to remember to ask. You don't have to remember to tell them. The system does both.
2. Group communication should not mean broadcast spam
WhatsApp groups are the default today, and they have a problem: everything is visible to everyone. Parents scroll through fifty messages to find the one about their child. Some see "fee reminder, please clear pending amounts" and feel singled out, even when it's a blanket message.
The alternative for sensitive or student-specific info is per-family delivery . Each parent sees only what concerns their own child — their attendance, their fees, their batch. That's harder to do manually and trivial with software, because the records already know who belongs to whom.
3. Cut the number of touchpoints rationally
You don't need to message parents every day. Over-communication becomes noise, and parents start ignoring you. A sane cadence looks like:
Automated: attendance summary, fee reminders, batch updates
Human: a call only for real concerns (repeated absence, behaviour)
Never: "please reply to confirm" messages with no purpose
One center owner told us they moved parents to automated updates for routine things and kept calls only for real issues. Their missed calls dropped from several a day to almost none in a month.
4. Give parents a record they can check anytime
Some parents don't want notifications at all — they want to check when they feel like it. A simple view where a parent can see payment history, attendance and batch details on their own schedule removes most of the "just checking" calls and questions.
The bottom line
Parent communication breaks when answers live inside your head or a single group chat. When updates go to parents automatically and questions get answered before they're asked, the phone stops ringing and parents trust you more.
Let parents self-serve instead of calling you
PingClass sends attendance and fee updates to each parent individually, and gives every parent their own view of their child's records.

PingClass vs Classplus: Which Tuition Management Software Fits Your Size?
Software · 6 min read · Updated September 2026
Classplus is the biggest name in Indian tuition management — a heavily funded platform that powers thousands of coaching institutes. PingClass is a small, self-funded alternative built around one idea: most institutes do not need most features. Which one fits depends on your size, your budget and how much complexity you actually want to run.
What Classplus does well
Branded app. Your institute gets its own branded app, which looks professional to parents and students.
Built-in payment gateway. Collect fees inside the platform — no separate payment setup or reconciliation.
Large user base. A big community, established brand and proven track record with thousands of institutes.
Robust course and fee features. Batch management, course catalogs, fee structures and reports built for scale.
India-focused. Pricing, payment methods, SMS and parent communication are all tuned to the Indian market.
Where Classplus costs more
Classplus is a serious product, and it is priced that way:
Pricing starts higher. The free or low tiers are limited; the plans that unlock real features cost more from day one.
Long-term contracts. You commit for a period, not month to month. That is a real risk for a small institute trying a tool for the first time.
Per-seat onboarding. Setup and onboarding are charged per seat, so the price climbs as your institute grows.
Features behind higher tiers. What you actually want is often gated behind a more expensive plan than you started with.
Complex for a two-teacher institute. Courses, catalogs, catalogs of catalogs — the depth becomes overhead when you just want attendance and fees.
None of that makes Classplus bad. It makes it a tool sized for a specific kind of institute — and small, simple centers pay for power they never use.
What PingClass does well
Free for up to 20 students. The free tier is a working product, not a trial — no time limit, no card required.
No contract. Month to month, simple paid plans, and you can walk away any time.
Attendance + fees + parent app in one place. The three things a small institute actually runs on, under one roof.
Simple setup. Sign up, add your batches, add students. You are running within the hour, with no onboarding calls.
Works globally. No Indian tax complexity baked in — the same dashboard works for an institute anywhere.
Where PingClass falls short
No branded mobile app for institutes. Parents use the parent app, but your institute does not get its own white-label app yet.
No payment gateway integration yet. Fees are tracked in the dashboard; collection still happens outside the tool.
Smaller community. Fewer institutes, fewer tutorials, less support content than a platform with Classplus's scale.
No enterprise SSO. If you need SAML and centralized login for a large chain, that capability is not there.
Side-by-side comparison
Feature Classplus PingClass
Pricing model Higher starting price, per-seat onboarding, long-term contracts Free for up to 20 students, simple month-to-month plans, no contract
Branded app Yes — your institute gets its own app No branded institute app yet
Payment gateway Built-in collection inside the platform Not integrated yet — track payments in the dashboard
Attendance Tracked within the app ecosystem Marked in seconds, batch-wise, visible to admins and parents
Fee tracking Full course catalogs and fee structures built for scale Paid, pending and overdue per student and per batch
Parent access Parent-facing communication and app access Parent app with attendance and payment history in one place
Batches Strong multi-batch, multi-course management Multiple batches, each with its own attendance and fees
Onboarding time Setup calls and per-seat onboarding process Sign up and start the same day — no onboarding calls
Contract required Long-term commitment No contract — cancel any time
The honest recommendation
Use Classplus if you are running 50+ students, want a branded app parents open on their phones, and want a payment gateway built into the product. The cost and the complexity are justified when the platform is doing real work at real scale.
Use PingClass if you are under 50 students, want to start free, and prefer simplicity over feature density. A two-teacher institute does not need a course catalog — it needs to know who came today and who has not paid.
Both tools are fine choices. Size is the real deciding factor — everything else is the platform that matches the size.
The bottom line
Classplus and PingClass solve the same problem at different scales. If you are growing toward 50+ students, Classplus earns its price. If you are small and want to stay simple, PingClass gets you the same core record — attendance, fees, parents — free, with no contract to escape.
Both tools are fine choices. PingClass is free for up to 20 students — see if the simplicity fits.
Attendance, fees and a parent app in one place. Free for up to 20 students, no time limit, no card required.

TOOLS
PingClass vs Spreadsheets and WhatsApp for Tuition Centers
6 min read · Updated September 2026
Almost every small tuition center runs on the same stack: a shared spreadsheet for students and fees, and a WhatsApp group for parents. It works — until it quietly stops working. This guide compares spreadsheets and WhatsApp against purpose-built tuition management software like PingClass, so you can see exactly when the switch pays for itself.
The short answer
Spreadsheets and WhatsApp are free and familiar, but they put the work on you: every attendance entry, every fee reminder, every "has Rahul paid?" is a manual task. Tuition management software keeps one shared record and automates the reminders and the views. Once two teachers are entering data, or parents start asking what they owe, purpose-built software stops being optional.
What spreadsheets actually do well
Zero cost. Free if you already pay for a Google account.
Total flexibility. You can structure a sheet however you like.
Familiar. No new tool to learn for a 20-student batch.
Same for WhatsApp: it's free, everyone has it, and it reaches parents instantly.
Where the free stack breaks down
The problems appear in stages, not all at once:
One person becomes the sheet. Attendance stops getting logged the moment the owner is busy teaching, because only they "own" the data.
WhatsApp buries information. "Fee reminders" live between memes and school notices. Parents genuinely miss them.
No per-batch truth. "Who owes money in Class IX?" means filtering a sheet and cross-checking a group — every single time.
No role separation. Teachers see (and can edit) everything, or you give them nothing.
Disputes. "I already paid in May!" is exhausting to argue without a per-parent record.
Side-by-side comparison
Daily task Spreadsheets / WhatsApp Tuition management software
Attendance Manual entry; depends on someone remembering Marked in seconds, batch-wise, automatically visible to admins and parents
Fee tracking Names and amounts in a sheet; reminders sent one-by-one Paid, pending and overdue per student and per batch
Reminders Manual WhatsApp/SMS messages Automatic notifications before the due date
Parent questions Answered by you, repeatedly Parents open their own attendance and payment history
Access control Everyone sees everything, or nobody Admin, teacher and parent each get their own view
Cost Free — paid for in evening hours ₹0–₹599/month depending on size
Not everyone needs to switch
Be honest with yourself:
One teacher, under ~20 students, and fee disputes almost never happen? A spreadsheet genuinely works.
The moment you're two or more teachers , tracking multiple batches , or fielding repeat fee questions — the manual stack costs you more than a subscription does.
Spreadsheets are the registration book of the internet age. They work because the institute is small enough that someone can babysit them.
What PingClass replaces, specifically
The attendance sheet — teachers mark from the dashboard, and the record lives once.
The "who owes what" sheet — paid, pending and overdue is computed per student and per batch.
The reminder walk — parents get push notifications before due dates; no SMS costs, no WhatsApp API.
The WhatsApp questions — a parent app the parent can check instead of calling you.
You keep the parent relationship . You stop being the human database behind it.
The bottom line
Use spreadsheets until there are two people touching the data. After that, measure the switch by time, not price: if the tool saves one evening a month, it has already paid for itself.
Keep the sheets, or try the system.
PingClass replaces the attendance sheet, the fee sheet and the WhatsApp question loop — free for up to 20 students, no time limit.

BATCHES
How to Structure Batches for a Tuition or Coaching Institute
5 min read · Updated September 2026
Batches are the skeleton of a coaching institute. Get them right and attendance, fees, and teacher workloads line up almost by themselves. Get them wrong and you're forever juggling "which student is in which group, again?"
Here's a practical way to structure batches that scales from 20 students to a few hundred.
1. Split by class and subject, not convenience
The most obvious dimensions — class (IX, X, XII) and subject (Maths, Science) — are usually the right ones. Students group naturally by what they're preparing for, and teachers specialize by subject.
Within that, a common mistake is packing everyone in one physical slot. If Monday 4:30 works for most, eager students get in and late joiners start a second, smaller batch. Size matters more than neatness:
1–10 students : near one-on-one, high fee per student
10–15 students : the sweet spot for attention and economics
16–25 students : fine for strong subjects with a good teacher; watch the weak students
25+ : you're basically a classroom now — expect attendance issues
2. Give every batch a single source of truth
Manual institutes keep a register per batch, a fee list per batch, and sometimes a WhatsApp group per batch — and they drift apart. "His fees are pending, no wait, he moved to Class X batch."
When a batch is a named entity that attendance, fees and announcements hang off — rather than a sheet of paper — every question about that batch has one answer.
3. Assign teachers per batch, then check the load
Attendance problems often start with teacher overload, not student apathy. Structure batches so each teacher's weekly load is visible:
How many batches does each teacher run?
What times conflict across batches?
Who is a weak student to the teacher we can't afford to overload?
A two-teacher academy we spoke to restructured around teacher load and cut cancellations from twice a week to zero in a month — because no teacher was double-booked anymore.
4. Fees attach to the batch, not the enrollment form
When every student in a batch pays the same monthly fee, collections become predictable. You can see at a glance: batch has 14 students × ₹1,500 = ₹21,000 expected. Then compare against what's been collected — the gap is your follow-up list.
The bottom line
Good batch structure is boring, and that's the point. Sized right, named clearly, taught by a manageable-load teacher, and carrying its own attendance and fee records — a batch that's structured this way runs itself.
Run batches that run themselves
PingClass keeps students, teachers, attendance and fees attached to the right batch — and shows collection rate per batch at a glance.

## Tuition Fees: Monthly Subscription vs Course Fee, Which is Better — PingClass Blog

Tuition Fees: Monthly Subscription vs Course Fee, Which is Better — PingClass Blog

← Back to Blog
FEES
Tuition Fees: Monthly Subscription vs Course Fee
4 min read · Updated September 2026
One of the first pricing decisions a tuition center makes is how to charge: per month, per term, or per course. There's no universal "right" answer — but there is a right answer for your situation. Here's the comparison.
Monthly fee (most common)
You charge a fixed amount each month, like ₹1,500, until the student stops. This is what most Indian tuition centers do.
Pros: predictable income; parents think of it as a small recurring cost; easy to adjust if the student changes batches.
Cons: you're chasing collection every single month; students can quietly stop paying while still attending.
Monthly works best when your coaching is open-ended — school-syllabus support that runs across the academic year.
Course fee / term fee
You charge a larger amount up front for a defined period: a 3-month term, or a fixed module (e.g. "Maths Class X — full year ₹9,000").
Pros: you get your money early, which means fewer reminders; parents commit properly; revenue per student is higher and predictable.
Cons: a bigger ticket is harder for parents to say yes to; seasonal exam-prep centers have a natural start/end anyway.
Term fees suit exam-focused programs (board prep, JEE/NEET crash courses) where there's a clear beginning and end.
Hybrid: monthly with a term commitment
Many centers strike a middle ground: collect a term or annual fee that includes a top-up for the full year, while letting monthly reminders fall away for everyone who's paid. This gives you the certainty of course fees and the flexibility parents expect day-to-day.
What the collection burden looks like in each model
Model Collection touchpoints / yr Typical loss
Monthly ~12 reminders per student 1–2 months lost per dropout
Term 2–4 per student Low — money up front
Hybrid 1–2 per student Lowest
Whatever model you choose, the mechanics matter more than the label: knowing exactly who's paid, who's pending, and sending one reminder before the due date is what actually protects your income.
The bottom line
Use monthly fees for ongoing school support, term or course fees for exam-oriented programs, and a hybrid if you can. Then make the collection process itself automatic so the model you pick doesn't fall apart in month two.
Whatever you charge, collect without chasing
PingClass tracks paid and pending fees per student and batch, sends reminders before the due date, and shows your real collection rate.

## Why Tally and Full ERPs Are Overkill for a Tuition Center — PingClass Blog

Why Tally and Full ERPs Are Overkill for a Tuition Center — PingClass Blog

Features
Pricing

← Back to Blog
SOFTWARE
Why Tally and Full ERPs Are Overkill for a Tuition Center
Software · 5 min read · Updated September 2026
Many tuition center owners hear "use Tally" or "implement an ERP" the moment they mention fee tracking. Tally is an excellent accounting tool, and ERP software genuinely runs factories and schools with 500+ staff. But neither was designed for a 30-student coaching center, and the mismatch shows up the first week you try to use them. Here is why a general accounting suite is the wrong tool for running an institute.
What Tally does well
Tally is a mature, genuinely capable accounting product. For a business with employees, inventory and compliance obligations, it handles the serious work:
GST compliance. Invoices, input credit reconciliation and returns are built-in and battle-tested.
Depth of accounting. Ledgers, balances, profit and loss, trial balance, audit trails — the full accounting core.
Inventory and stock. Items, godowns and valuation for businesses that physically hold goods.
Payroll. Salary structures and pay runs when you have a real employee list.
None of these are small jobs. If you sell stock, file GST and pay a staff of twenty, Tally earns its place.
Why Tally is wrong for a tuition center
The problem is not that Tally is a bad product. It is that a tuition center is a different kind of business, and the areas Tally ignores are exactly where the institute runs:
No student-level attendance view. Tally tracks money, not people. You cannot mark "present" per student per class, let alone see the trending absentees in a batch at a glance.
No parent portal. There is no interface where a parent opens their child's attendance and payment history. Every question is answered by you, on the phone.
No batch-wise fee tracking. Tally records fee payments as journal entries. "Who owes what in Class IX evening batch" is not a question Tally can answer with one click.
No automatic reminders. There is no concept of a due date that pings a parent before it passes. Reminders remain a manual job.
A steep learning curve. The person using it is usually a teacher who has been teaching four hours a day. Voucher entry and account masters are not how they think, and they should not have to.
What an ERP actually solves
"ERP" sounds impressive until you read the feature list, because the features it stresses are the problems a tuition center simply does not have:
Multi-department inventory. Raw material, work-in-progress and finished goods across locations.
HR and attendance for staff. Leave policies, payroll integration and heads for hundreds of employees.
Procurement and vendor management. Purchase orders, vendor ledgers and purchasing workflows.
Large-school administration. Timetabling, exam systems and departments for institutions that run like organisations.
These are the problems of a factory, a distributor or a 500-student coaching chain. A 30-student center has none of them, so most of the ERP is overhead — screens to click through, modules to license and training to pay for, all hunting for problems the institute does not own.
What a tuition center actually needs
Strip away the departments and the institute really runs on four things:
Batch-wise attendance. Mark a class for Class IX in seconds; everyone else can see it without being asked.
Student-wise fee status. Paid, pending and overdue — visible per student and per batch, without opening a ledger.
Parent notifications. Reminders reach parents automatically before the due date, instead of living in a manual to-do list.
A dashboard a teacher can use in 30 seconds. The person in front of the class should not need an accounting course to record that a student attended.
Dedicated tuition management software was built around exactly these four problems. That is the whole point of it: the features line up with the job before you, instead of asking the job to bend around an accounting package.
Side-by-side comparison
Feature Tally / General ERP Tuition management software
Primary purpose Accounting, inventory and organisational administration Running the institute — attendance, fees, parents
Attendance per student Not available; tracks money and stock, not people Marked per student per class, batch-wise, instantly
Batch tracking Manual bookkeeping that you label yourself Built in: fees and attendance grouped by batch
Parent portal None Parents open their own attendance and payment history
Fee reminders None; manual follow-up Automatic notifications before the due date
Setup time Chart of accounts, masters, configuration; days to weeks Add students and batches; usable within an hour
Monthly cost Licence plus training and often a consultant; thousands ₹0–₹599/month depending on size
GST invoicing Excellent — the genuine reason to own it Focused on fee receipts; general GST is your accountant's job
The exception
The exception is a larger coaching institute that already runs like a small business: employees on payroll, physical inventory (books, material, uniforms) and real GST obligations. In that case Tally can make sense for the accounting side — your accountant should be happy in it.
But Tally still does not replace attendance, parent access or batch tracking. If you grow into an ERP, you pair it with tuition management software — you do not swap one for the other.
Bottom line
Do not use a general tool for a specialised job. Tally is for accounting, and it is excellent at it. Tuition software is for running the institute — attendance, fees, parents and reminders — and it is excellent at that. The two do not compete; they simply answer different questions. For the day-to-day of a tuition center, the tool built for it is the one that fits.
Choose the tool that fits the job
When the advice is "just use Tally," ask what you are actually tracking: ledgers, or students? If the answer is students, the accounting suite was never the right hangar for that plane.
Tuition software handles what Tally was never built for.
PingClass is free for up to 20 students, no time limit. Attendance, fee status and parent notifications without the ledger entry.

Privacy Policy
Last updated: 6 September 2026
PingClass ("we", "our", "us") provides fee management software for tuition centers and coaching institutes. This Privacy Policy explains what personal data we process, why, and the rights you have under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (the "DPDP Act") of India.
हिन्दी में मुख्य बातें (एक नज़र में)
हम आपके व्यक्तिगत डेटा को कम से कम और केवल आवश्यक उद्देश्यों के लिए संसाधित (process) करते हैं। हम आपका डेटा बेचते नहीं हैं।
18 वर्ष से कम उम्र के बच्चों के डेटा के लिए माता-पिता/अभिभावक की सत्यापन योग्य सहमति आवश्यक है। हम बच्चों के डेटा का विपणन (marketing) या निगरानी (tracking) नहीं करते।
आपको अपने डेटा तक पहुँचने, उसे सुधारने, निर्यात (export) करने और मिटाने (delete) का अधिकार है।
किसी भी प्रश्न या शिकायत के लिए हमसे pingclassoff@gmail.com पर संपर्क करें।
1. Who processes your data
In most cases the institute (tuition center) that uses PingClass is the Data Fiduciary in respect of student and parent data entered into the platform. PingClass acts as a Data Processor on the institute's instructions. In respect of your PingClass account (name, email, login), PingClass is itself the Data Fiduciary.
2. Data we collect and process
Account data — name, email address and password (securely stored) when you create a PingClass account.
Institute data — institute name, contact email, phone number and address, entered to set up your profile.
Student and parent data — names, phone numbers, batch assignments, attendance, fee records and parent links, entered by the institute into the platform.
Payment data — fee/subscription payment records. Card details are handled directly by our payment provider (Razorpay); we do not store card numbers.
Technical data — basic usage data needed to operate and secure the service.
Analytics data — aggregated, anonymized visitor statistics (such as pages visited and general region) collected via Google Analytics to understand how the site is used and to improve it. IP addresses are anonymized before being sent to Google, and this data is not used to identify or profile individual visitors.
3. Why we process data
To create and manage your account and provide the PingClass service.
To record and manage fees, attendance, batches and announcements at your institute's direction.
To process payments through our payment provider.
To communicate service-related notices and, with consent, relevant updates.
To protect the security of the service and comply with law.
We rely on your consent (for example, when you create an account) and on the legitimate uses permitted under Section 7 of the DPDP Act, including performance of the services you request and fulfilling legal obligations.
4. Children's data
PingClass is a business tool used by institutes. Where student data entered into the platform relates to children below 18 years of age, the institute is responsible, as Data Fiduciary, for obtaining verifiable parental consent before processing such data. We do not profile children, do not use their data for behavioural monitoring, and do not market to children.
5. How we protect data
Data is transmitted over encrypted connections and stored in a managed, access-controlled database. Access to records is governed by role-based permissions (admin, teacher, parent) and row-level security. We do not sell personal data.
6. Who we share data with
Razorpay — to process payments. Only the information needed for the transaction is shared.
Hosting / service providers — infrastructure operators that store or transmit data on our behalf under appropriate agreements.
Where data must be transferred outside India, we ensure such transfers comply with the safeguards required by the DPDP Act.
7. Your rights
Under the DPDP Act, you (and, where applicable, the parents/guardians of students) may:
Access — obtain a summary of your personal data held in the platform.
Correct — update inaccurate or incomplete information.
Erase — request deletion of your data, subject to legal and financial-record obligations.
Withdraw consent — where processing is based on consent.
Complain — to us first, and thereafter to the Data Protection Board of India.
Contact the institute managing your data for student or parent records. For your PingClass account, contact us at the address below.
8. Retention
Account data — We keep your PingClass account, institute profile, and associated student records for as long as your account is active. Student, batch, and announcement records are soft-deleted (retained with restricted access) to preserve audit trails and financial records.
Payment records — While your account is active, fee and subscription payment records are retained for 6 years as required by Indian tax law (Income Tax Act 1961, s.44AA / Rule 6F; GST Act 2017, s.36); after that they are deleted.
Full account deletion — On full account deletion, all personal data — including payment records — is permanently removed from the platform.
Audit logs — Records of data changes (audit logs) are kept for 12 months and then deleted by an automated job.
Invite tokens — Invitation tokens that were used are kept for 90 days to support resending OTPs. Unused, expired tokens are purged after 30 days.
Scheduled cleanup — A daily automated job cleans up stale invite tokens, orphaned link rows, and expired audit logs. No personal data is retained longer than necessary.
9. Security incidents
In the unlikely event of a data breach affecting your data, we will notify you and the Data Protection Board of India within the timeframes required by the DPDP Act.
10. Grievance
If you have a privacy concern, please contact us. We will respond within the period required under the DPDP Act and its Rules.
Grievance Officer / Contact
PingClass
Email: pingclassoff@gmail.com
Response target: within 7 business days.
11. Changes to this policy
We may update this policy from time to time. The "Last updated" date above reflects the latest version. Significant changes will be communicated through the app.

Terms of Service
Last updated: 14 August 2026
These Terms of Service ("Terms") govern your use of the PingClass platform ("PingClass", "we", "our"). By creating an account or using the service, you agree to these Terms and to our Privacy Policy .
1. The service
PingClass provides fee management, student, attendance and communication tools for tuition centers and coaching institutes. Features may vary by plan as shown on our pricing page.
2. Accounts
You must provide accurate information when creating an account.
You are responsible for safeguarding your login credentials and for activity under your account.
Accounts may be assigned admin, teacher or parent roles with different permissions.
You must be at least 18 years of age to create an account. If you create an account on behalf of an organization, you represent that you are authorized to bind it.
3. Institute responsibilities and data
In respect of student and parent data you enter, your institute is the Data Fiduciary under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023. You agree to:
Provide a privacy notice to students and parents before their data is collected through PingClass.
Obtain verifiable parental consent before processing data of children below 18 years of age.
Use data only for the purposes for which it was collected, and honour requests for access, correction and erasure.
Only enter data you are lawfully entitled to process.
PingClass processes this data as a Data Processor on your instructions, as further described in our Privacy Policy.
4. Acceptable use
You will not misuse the service, attempt to access data you are not authorized to see, or interfere with the platform.
You will not upload unlawful or infringing content.
You will not resell the service without our written consent.
5. Fees and payments
Paid plans are billed through our payment provider (Razorpay). Fees are as described on the pricing page at the time of purchase. You authorize us to charge the applicable fees. Refunds, if any, are handled on a case-by-case basis.
6. Intellectual property
The PingClass software, design and content are owned by PingClass and are protected by law. We grant you a limited, non-exclusive, non-transferable right to use the service for your internal purposes. Your data remains yours.
7. Availability and liability
We aim to keep the service available and reliable but do not guarantee uninterrupted or error-free operation.
The service is provided "as is". To the maximum extent permitted by law, our total liability for any claim is limited to the fees you paid in the six months before the claim.
Nothing in these Terms limits liability that cannot be excluded by law.
8. Security incidents
If a data breach affects your data, we will notify you in line with the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 and help you meet your notification obligations.
9. Termination
You may stop using the service and close your account at any time.
We may suspend or terminate access for breach of these Terms, with notice where practicable.
On termination, your data will be deleted or returned as you direct, subject to legal obligations.
10. Changes to these Terms
We may update these Terms from time to time. Continued use of the service after changes take effect constitutes acceptance. The "Last updated" date above reflects the latest version.
11. Governing law
These Terms are governed by the laws of India. Disputes will be subject to the jurisdiction of the courts of India.
12. Contact
Questions about these Terms? Email us at pingclassoff@gmail.com .
